Better Off Ted

Crap title and poorly marketed, but it's a fantastic workplace comedy.
The Golden Girls. The show remained funny throughout, even if the earlier seasons are arguably better.

I just finished watching Wonder Man, I was a little bit on the fence on starting it since I heard it was a little divisive. I ended up really liking it. Might even be in my top 3 Marvel shows. I'm not too familiar with Wonder Man so the amount it was true to the comics or the lack of big flashy fights didn't really bother me. Yahya Abdul-Mateen II and Ben Kingsley were both amazing. And it's an unpopular opinion but I was a big fan of Ironman 3 so I loved the return of Kingsley as the "fake" Mandarin. I'd watch him in that role for hours. I'm sad it got cancelled, would have really liked to see more of Simon and Trevor's story. Maybe he'll show up in one of the movies but I would be surprised if he wasn't relegated to anything but a very small role. It's a shame.

I'd say Schitt's Creek. For the Roses at least. Especially Alexis who starts out as the typical Paris Hilton socialite trope and turns into a really grounded self-assured character. But even Moria goes from melodramatic screams over everything to behaving like an actual person sometimes in later seasons.

In a show with a real budget they would've had a much bigger conflict at the whitehouse and the GenV characters would've been fighting through the other supes so Butcher and gang had a shot at homelander. For some reason in the actual show there was like 2 people other than homelander in the whole whitehouse.

War. It’s good, nothing amazing yet but it feels like it will be a good show and there’s not many good shows out right now.

Dark Matter S2. I don’t know what’s going on and I don’t know if I care enough to learn from S1. But it’s watchable
Call the Midwife! Still going on, has plateaued a bit (and COVID restrictions seem to have been onerous) but still overally excellent, and IMO their best cast wasn't even the original cast.
What is with people hating everything these days? The last season was still pretty good.

First few episodes are rough and slow. Production is not as strong as most other shows in those episodes. I think everything gets better though, and by the second season, I really enjoyed it. Actors and character development are good throughoutThey spend a good deal of time on the Sanhedrin and the Romans, to show their motives and give the needed historical context to understand the story. The writers have said they were influenced by The Wire (my all-time favorite drama), and while it's... not that show, you can see it sometimes in how they try to cover "all sides" and explain the systems of that time period. The writing can actually be pretty funny at times too
Bojack Horseman did a great job developing characters

I'd say Bob's Burgers is a good example of this. The characterization jump from the first season, to that Christmas episode they just did, is crazy. As the show went on and found its voice as a more understated and (usually) wholesome comedy, the characters were allowed to become less exaggerated, and consequently more human and relatable.

i'm just about at the end of the 6th ep.! the 5th ep. was so good! the recreated scenes with Claudette and Barry (from the original film) in that ep. are freaking well done! they had me actually clapping and smiling big time! it convinced me Kane & Co. took great care and put a lot of love into all those scenes and this series overall! i loved and was also really impressed with the scenes of "Annie" walking through the town, into the diner, etc. in Ep. 4 (also just like in the original film!) were also fantastic too!
i admit i'm not in love with everything thus far. i could do without the screen time spent on Officer Dorf but there's a lot to really like/love about it especially if one is an F13 fan.

This show is terrible but if they wanted to run it for 15 years, so be it. One half hour a week on a channel I barely watch, that doesn't affect me. But for the love of God I need TBS to get rid of the syndication rights, there was a stretch there where they were cutting back on Seinfeld episodes for 2 Broke Girls, that hurt my soul
A lot of the classics. Taxi, Cheers, and Frasier come to mind as a few of the really good ones.

Mr. InBetween - It's on FX/Hulu in the US. An Australian crime show that actually does the "criminal with a heart of gold" thing really, really well. Well acted, well written, and compelling the entire time. It's an easy watch too - 3 relatively quick seasons, episodes are ~30 minutes, and a complete, satisfying story that never really drags.

I'd say this is for fans of Sons of Anarchy, Breaking Bad (imagine a series based around Mike), etc.

I  actually enjoy the 1st season because Michael is so awful. But it is probably the weakest season. It does definitely get better. Michael is still super cringe and awkward, but you learn that he isn't a bad guy.
This show was worse than Big Bang. It was just sex jokes and racial stereotypes, terribly done. I can't believe it lasted 6 seasons.

I don't know if it's obscure, but I wish Forever got a few more seasons, Ioan Gruffudd as the immortal Medical Examiner was just good fun.

Some more Hornblower episodes/telemovies would be good too come to think of it
Limited the viewership then be surprised by reduced viewership is diabolical insanity.

The only people equipped to handle The Dark Tower would have been David Lynch and David Cronenberg. Simultaneously directing different scenes of the series without consulting one another, then editing them together at random.
I am not a big fan of the franchise. It might be the reason that I like the series so far. I am 3 episodes in. I love Linda. Think she was a perfect cast.

Death in Paradise. The entire cast has changed several times at this point, but overall the series is still just as strong as it was at the start.It helps that its main appeals are setting and the Agatha Christie-esq mysteries.

Fantasy shows do come out but the cost of them is usually higher. But there is more game of thrones spinoffs to come this year and Percy Jackson. There is a bunch of anime that would count. Interview with a vampire. Small Prophets (low fantasy).If you liked Half Bad, may be try Lockwood and Co, it feels like a Saturday kids show but it is really good. It is on Netflix.

diagnosis murder was already a spin off! I used to watch it as a kid, years later saw a random episode of jake and the fat man (had never even heard of it tbh) that turned out to be the diagnosis murder backdoor pilot. guess it worked once and they got cocky
